_note: UNFAIR -- Hard's plan with a head start and no hesitation (AI_Player_difficulty.md).
THE RULES ARE HARD'S, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. The difficulty table gives Unfair the
same four lines as Hard -- strong economy, attacks once established, age 4, towers
and castles -- and adds exactly one thing: 'starts with 8 villagers and 2 swordsmen
and 1 scout'. So the cheat is the START, not the thinking, which is what the word
'unfair' should mean. A bot that also played better would be two changes wearing
one name, and nobody could tell you afterwards which one made it hard.
IT DECLARES THE DIFFERENCE, NOT THE TOTAL, and the scout is why that is worth
saying. The table asks for '8 villagers and 2 swordsmen and 1 scout'; every player
already starts with 5 villagers and a scout, so what belongs here is +3 villagers
and +2 swordsmen and NO scout. Declaring the scout gave Unfair two of them, which
the test caught -- and it is exactly the kind of thing that would otherwise ship as
a bot that is mysteriously better at scouting than the table says.
start_units IS THE ONLY THING IN ANY OF THESE FILES THAT IS NOT A RULE. It is a
handicap applied once by SimWorld.setup(), not a decision the AI makes, and it is
here rather than in the map or the lobby because it belongs to the DIFFICULTY --
the same map has to be playable against Easy.
THE EXTRA VILLAGERS ARE WORTH MORE THAN THE SOLDIERS, and it is worth knowing which
way round that is before tuning it. Eight villagers against the usual five is a
~60% opening economy lead that compounds for the whole match; two swordsmen and a
scout is a raid that trades once. If Unfair ever feels merely annoying rather than
hard, the villagers are the number to move.
lag_ticks IS [0, 0] -- it acts on the tick its conditions come true. Every other
level draws a delay to model a human noticing late; this one does not pretend.
